section_1.title: Prerequisite: The Static Slope
section_1.content: Establish the foundation by visualizing a straight line on a graph. Define the slope as 'rise over run' (Δy/Δx), representing a constant rate of change.
section_1.example: A turtle crawling at a steady pace: the constant steepness of its path on a coordinate grid.

section_2.title: The Problem of Curvature
section_2.content: Introduce a curve (non-linear function). Explain that the slope is no longer constant. We need a way to measure the 'instantaneous steepness' at a single point.
section_2.example: A mountain goat climbing a curved cliffside; its steepness changes with every step it takes.

section_3.title: The Zooming Transformation (Secant to Tangent)
section_3.content: Visualize the secant line passing through two points (P and Q). Show an animation where point Q moves closer to P until the distance Δx becomes infinitesimally small. The secant transforms into the tangent line.
section_3.example: An animated camera zooming into a curved track until the small section of the track appears as a straight line (the tangent).

section_4.title: Defining the Derivative as an Operator
section_4.content: Formally introduce the derivative as a transformation: it takes a function f(x) and maps it to a new function f'(x) that outputs the slope at any input x.
section_4.example: A 'magic box' machine: Input the curve equation, and it outputs a new 'slope-graph' showing how steep the mountain is at every position.

section_5.title: Synthesis: Dynamic Interpretation
section_5.content: Conclude by shifting the perspective from 'static geometry' to 'dynamic motion.' The derivative is the rate of change of the state of a system.
section_5.example: A rocket launching: The position graph is the path, while the derivative (slope) is the instantaneous velocity at any given second.

        p_x, q_x = -1.0, 1.0
        p_point = Dot(axes.c2p(p_x, 0.5 * p_x**2), color="#FF0000")
        q_point = Dot(axes.c2p(q_x, 0.5 * q_x**2), color="#FF0000")
        
        secant = Line(p_point.get_center(), q_point.get_center(), color=WHITE)
        
        # Setup trackers
        q_tracker = ValueTracker(q_x)
        
        def update_secant(l):
            new_q = axes.c2p(q_tracker.get_value(), 0.5 * q_tracker.get_value()**2)
            q_point.move_to(new_q)
            l.put_start_and_end_on(p_point.get_center(), new_q)
            
        secant.add_updater(update_secant)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(p_point), FadeIn(q_point), Create(secant))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FF0000")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===

        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFF00")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===

        self.play(graph_group.animate.scale(2.5), run_time=2)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FF00")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        secant.remove_updater(update_secant)
        tangent = Line(axes.c2p(-1, 0.5), axes.c2p(0, 0), color="#00FFFF")
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(secant, tangent))
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#00FFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        label = Text("Tangent", color="#00FFFF", font_size=24)
        self.place_at_grid(label, 'F3')
        self.play(Write(label))
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#00FFFF")

        self.wait(2)

    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Zooming Transformation (Secant to Tangent)", [
            "Secant line connects two points.",
            "Moving points closer reduces distance.",
            "Zooming reveals a straight line.",
            "Secant transforms into a tangent.",
            "Tangent shows instantaneous slope."
        ])

        # Define Curve: y = 0.5 * x^2
        axes = Axes(x_range=[-2, 2], y_range=[-0.5, 2], axis_config={"include_tip": False})
        curve = axes.plot(lambda x: 0.5 * x**2, color=WHITE)

        secant = Line(p_point.get_center(), q_point.get_center(), color=WHITE)
        
        # Setup trackers
        q_tracker = ValueTracker(q_x)
        
        def update_secant(l):
            new_q = axes.c2p(q_tracker.get_value(), 0.5 * q_tracker.get_value()**2)
            q_point.move_to(new_q)
            l.put_start_and_end_on(p_point.get_center(), new_q)
